editorial.headline: Conventional Office-Building Construction, Open Nationally and Workable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 41012 covers conventional construction, upkeep, rebuilding, alteration, and renovation of office buildings, including offices and rukan.
editorial.body:
KBLI 41012 is a construction activity for office buildings built by conventional methods. The slim record defines the scope around the building, maintenance, and rebuilding of office premises, with the same line also covering alteration and renovation. In practical terms, this is not a general property or office-use category; it is the activity of constructing and working on office buildings themselves, including ordinary offices and rumah kantor, or rukan.

The record also anchors this activity in the construction subclassification language: GT002 and BG002 are both named for office-building construction. That matters because the activity is framed as a construction line, not simply as real-estate ownership, office management, or commercial tenancy. A company using this activity should therefore be describing the work of putting up, maintaining, rebuilding, changing, or renovating office-building assets through conventional construction methods.

On scale, the record is broad. It is open to Besar, Menengah, Kecil, and Mikro. That means the activity is not presented here as only a large-contractor field, even though the foreign-investment reading naturally pays close attention to the Besar scale. The editorial point is simple: the activity can be registered across the full scale range shown in the record, but the investor profile still has to be read through the national PMA status and the Bali-side screening note.

Nationally, the record marks KBLI 41012 as TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100. The clean reading is that the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. Instead, Bali is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not blocked on the Bali field supplied here. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a hidden Bali cap; it is a nationally open activity that the record does not mark as moratorium-blocked in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is not a hidden Bali cap, but a nationally open construction activity that the record does not mark as moratorium-blocked.
